title: Interactive Flexbox playground
learningObjectives: Explain interactive flexbox playground and build a responsive layout with it.

understand.concept: A Flexbox playground exposes controls for direction, wrapping, justify-content, align-items, align-content, gap, and item-level grow/shrink/basis. A good lab updates one visual model and clearly labels container controls separately from item controls.
understand.whyItMatters: The playground should keep control state and rendered output synchronized, provide keyboard-accessible controls, and include responsive testing. It should avoid suggesting that one set of values is correct for every layout.
understand.analogy: A playground is a small layout workbench: each control changes a known property and the preview shows the result.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual layout follows the flex or grid formatting algorithm.

explain.narrative: This starter demonstrates a flex preview with wrap, distribution, alignment, and gap. The interactive controls are the independent build task.

examples.explanation: This starter demonstrates a flex preview with wrap, distribution, alignment, and gap. The interactive controls are the independent build task.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered layout demonstrating the lesson concept.

practise.guidedTask: Add select controls for flex-direction, flex-wrap, justify-content, and align-items plus a range input for gap. Keep the preview updated and display the selected CSS declarations.
practise.independentTask: Build a small responsive interface using the concept. Test long labels and more than one viewport width.
hints: Inspect the layout overlay in developer tools.
Change one container or item property at a time.
Check for overflow and preserve reading order.
